This has been on my mind lately.

I have:

  • a desktop computer
  • a laptop
  • an external hard drive
  • a portable hard drive

On both my desktop and laptop, I have two partitions:

  1. Windows OS partition: system files, and global program files.
  2. Encrypted partition: all my personal files and my portable applications that store personal information, like Firefox, Thunderbird, etc.

The second partition (encrypted) is backed up on both the external and the portable hard drive for both the desktop and laptop. In the case of an emergency, I store my laptop and one of the drives in a case next to the door. All of my encrypted files are synced on all four mediums, so I wouldn't lose anything except the hardware.

I used to encrypt the entire hard drives, but I felt like it would be more secure having only a partition encrypted in case I need to force a dismount (re-encrypt) without having to shut down the computer.

I've been thinking about the future of portability and how it would be cool if I can store an entire encrypted operating system on a portable medium. I know it can (partially) be done with a Linux distro, but I use a lot of Windows programs, so I guess I'll have to wait for now.
